content: Q2 fiscal 2027 total revenue reached a record $96 billion, more than doubling year-over-year, with growth accelerating for the fourth consecutive quarter.
Q3 revenue is guided to $108 billion (plus or minus 2%), with Vera Rubin expected to account for about 20% of data center revenue.
Management guided fiscal 2028 revenue growth of approximately 70%, describing it as supply-constrained since unconstrained demand points to roughly 100% (doubling) growth.
Gross margins are being reset lower due to extreme memory pricing, with Q3 expected at 74%, bottoming at 71-72% in Q4, then settling at 72-73% in fiscal 2028.
Q2 data center revenue rose 18% sequentially to $89 billion, with hyperscale at $49 billion (up 13% QoQ) and AC I&E at $40 billion (up 25% QoQ and 138% YoY).
NVIDIA's revenue opportunity per gigawatt has expanded from ~$18 billion with Hopper to $25 billion with Blackwell to $40 billion with Vera Rubin, and is expected to rise further.

NVIDIA has invested nearly $50 billion in Frontier AI labs and partnered with six capital providers (Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs, KKR) to raise over $500 billion in third-party financing.
AWS is deploying an additional 2 million GPUs from this quarter through Q2 fiscal 2029, and AWS begins receiving Vera CPU shipments this quarter.

The company expects demand from AI labs that leverage NVIDIA's balance sheet to contribute roughly one-quarter of next year's business, while non-hyperscaler AC I&E will represent about half of data center revenue.
China data center compute revenue is excluded from the forward outlook, with Q2 Hopper 200 shipments to China representing less than 1% of data center revenue and being dilutive to gross margins.

# NVIDIA (NVDA) — Q2 FY2027 Earnings Preview

**Report date/time:** Wednesday, August 26, 2026, ~4:20 pm ET (20:20 UTC), after the close · Call at 5:00 pm ET
**Stock:** ~$212.51 · Market cap ~$5.24T · 52-week range $164.07–$236.54 (~10% below the high)
**Estimates as of:** Aug 21–26, 2026 (sources noted per line; consensus varies by provider)

---

## 1. Consensus Estimates

| Metric | Company Guidance (May 2026) | Consensus | Buy-Side / Whisper |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Revenue** | $91.0B ±2% ($89.2–92.8B) | **$91.9–92.3B** (41–60 analysts) | **$94–95B** |
| **EPS** | — | **$2.06 GAAP / $2.08–2.09 non-GAAP** | ~$2.15+ |
| **Data Center rev** | — | **~$85.7B** (range $83.5–91.5B, Visible Alpha) | high-$80s |
| **Gross margin** | 74.9% GAAP / 75.0% non-GAAP ±50bp | ~75% | ≥75%, no dilution from Rubin ramp |
| **GAAP opex** | ~$8.5B | ~$8.5B | — |
| **Q3 FY27 rev guide** | — | **$103.8–104.1B** | **$105B+** |
| **Q3 FY27 EPS** | — | $2.37 | — |

**Comps (Q1 FY27 actual):** Revenue $81.6B (+85% y/y, +20% q/q); Data Center $75.246B (+92% y/y, +21% q/q); Edge Computing $6.369B (+29% y/y); networking *within* DC $14.8B (+199% y/y). Consensus revenue implies **~+96–98% y/y** vs. the $46.7B year-ago quarter.

⚠️ **Two framing notes.** (1) NVIDIA restructured reporting in FY2027 into **Data Center** and **Edge Computing** — the old standalone Gaming / ProViz / Auto / OEM lines are not directly comparable, and I could not find reliable standalone Gaming or Networking consensus for the quarter. (2) Guidance **excludes all China data center compute revenue**, so any China contribution is upside to the guide, not embedded in it.

---

## 2. Key Metrics to Watch (ranked)

1. **Q3 FY27 revenue guidance** — the only number that really matters. Street is at ~$104B. The market is treating **$105B as the bull line and $103B as the disappointment line**. Guidance relative to the buy-side bar, not the size of the Q2 beat, has driven the last four reactions.
2. **Non-GAAP gross margin (and the FY27 mid-70s commitment)** — guided ~75%. A slip **toward 73% or below** would be read as pricing pressure from custom ASICs and would overshadow a revenue beat. Watch Rubin ramp costs and HBM/CoWoS input pricing.
3. **Data Center composition** — Hyperscale vs. ACIE (AI Cloud/Industrial/Enterprise) was ~50/50 in Q1. Continued ACIE broadening is the anti-concentration proof point; re-concentration into a few hyperscalers is a quality-of-earnings negative.
4. **Vera Rubin ramp** — management flagged Q3 shipment start, a "$200B new TAM" for Vera CPU and "nearly $20B in total CPU revenue this year." Any slip in timing, yields, or supply is a direct hit to the Q3/Q4 curve. Also watch for Blackwell→Rubin transition air-pocket commentary.
5. **China / H200** — U.S. approved H200 exports with conditions; ByteDance and Tencent each reportedly took ~10,000 H200s in the weeks before Aug 18, but Chinese import approvals are reportedly capped below 200K units. Watch whether management **re-includes China in Q3 guidance** — that alone could be worth several billion.
6. **Inference mix and backlog/supply commentary** — "tokens are now profitable" agentic-AI framing; any quantified visibility (multi-quarter booked demand) supports the durability case.
7. **Capital returns** — $80B buyback, ~50% of FCF targeted for return this year. Pace of repurchase is a soft signal on management's own valuation view.

---

## 3. Scenario Analysis

| Scenario | Revenue | Non-GAAP EPS | Q3 Guide | Key Driver | Est. Stock Reaction |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Bull (~25%)** | $95–97B | $2.18–2.25 | **≥$106–108B** | Rubin pulled forward, GM held ≥75%, China re-included in guide, ACIE broadening | **+6% to +11%** |
| **Base (~50%)** | $93–94.5B | $2.12–2.16 | **$104–105.5B** | Normal $2–3B beat-and-raise; GM ~75%; China still excluded | **−3% to +3%** |
| **Bear (~25%)** | $91–92.5B | $2.05–2.10 | **≤$103B** | Guide merely in line, GM drifting to ~73.5%, supply or Rubin-transition caution | **−8% to −13%** |

**What each requires operationally**
- **Bull:** Data Center ≥$89B with networking again growing triple digits; explicit statement that Rubin is shipping on/ahead of schedule at target margins; China DC compute added back to guidance.
- **Base:** Data Center $85–87B; the ~$2–3B beat Jefferies and others have been modeling; management reiterates mid-70s FY27 margin without raising the trajectory.
- **Bear:** Any of — guidance below $103B, gross margin guided below 74%, hedged language on Rubin timing, or an admission that hyperscaler order timing is lumpy into 2027.

**Historical context — the "beat and retreat" pattern.** NVDA has beaten on revenue, EPS *and* guidance for **four consecutive quarters and fallen the next day every time**, on an average beat of ~4.8%. Reported day-after moves cluster small and negative (roughly −0.5% to −5.5% depending on source; the series varies by provider, so treat the exact figures as approximate). The read-through: **the bar is the buy-side number, not the sell-side number**, and an in-line-to-modest beat has repeatedly been sold.

---

## 4. Catalyst Checklist

1. **Q3 revenue guide vs. $105B** — the single highest-beta variable. Above $105B validates that growth is running ahead of already-aggressive 2027 hyperscaler capex forecasts ($935B consensus, up to $1.2–1.45T from Goldman/UBS); below $103B feeds the deceleration narrative.
2. **Q2 revenue vs. the $94–95B whisper** (not the $92B print consensus) — clearing $92B is table stakes; the differentiated outcome is $95B+.
3. **Gross margin ≥75% and reaffirmed mid-70s for FY27** — the moat metric. Compression is the cleanest bear proof-point on custom-silicon competition.
4. **China guidance treatment** — re-inclusion of China DC compute in Q3 guidance is a genuine narrative shift and the most underpriced upside lever, given it's currently a zero in the model.
5. **Rubin/Vera ramp specifics** — units, customers, timing, margin profile. First-quarter-of-ramp commentary sets the FY28 slope.

---

## 5. Trading Setup

- **Options-implied move:** **±5.4% to ±5.9%** for the first full session after the print (sources differ; ~$280–286B of market cap at stake). Implied is **below** the ~7.4% average absolute post-earnings move over the trailing 12 quarters — but the last four *realized* moves were mostly under ~2%, so recent realized has undershot implied. Straddle buyers need a genuine tail outcome; that setup has lost money four quarters running.
- **Price action into the print:** ~$212.51, roughly 10% off the $236.54 52-week high, with the stock chopping lower into the event (−1.4% the prior session). Beta ~2.2 amplifies any downside.
- **Positioning/sentiment:** semiconductor funds saw ~$6.3B of cumulative outflows over three weeks; BofA's Bull & Bear Indicator at an extreme 9.5 (contrarian sell signal). Sentiment is *not* euphoric into the number — that's a mild positive for skew.
- **Implication:** implied move (~5.5%) sits below my bull and bear scenario magnitudes (+6–11% / −8–13%) and above my base case (−3% to +3%). If you have conviction in a tail, options look reasonably priced; if you expect another in-line beat-and-drift, the base case is well inside the straddle and premium selling is favored.

---

### Caveats

Consensus figures differ by provider ($91.85B / $91.9B / $92.07B / $92.28B revenue; $2.06 GAAP vs. $2.08–2.09 non-GAAP EPS) — I've shown ranges rather than a false-precision single number, and the GAAP/non-GAAP distinction is not consistently labeled across sources. Segment-level consensus below the Data Center line is thin because of the FY27 reporting change. Published post-earnings reaction histories conflict, so those percentages are directional. Several inputs come from secondary aggregators rather than primary sell-side notes; anything you'd trade on should be re-checked against your own data terminal. Finally — this reports **today at 4:20 pm ET**, so this preview has a short shelf life.

content: Enterprise net sales grew 5% in constant currency (top end of 4%-5% guidance), while adjusted operating income rose 17.4% and adjusted EPS increased over 19%.

Q2 operating income included a ~750 basis point benefit from approximately $2.9 billion in tariff refunds (about 0.5% of annual U.S. net sales), which management is reinvesting into price; excluding this, underlying OI growth was at the top end of the 7%-10% guidance.

Global e-commerce net sales grew 23%, with Walmart U.S. up 24% (tenth consecutive quarter above 20%), Sam's Club U.S. up 26%, and International up 19%, while U.S. e-commerce reached double-digit incremental margins in the first half.
Walmart U.S. comp sales rose only 2.6%, hurt by a 125 basis point drag from maximum fair price drug regulation, with management framing underlying core comps closer to 3.5%.
Full-year sales guidance was raised to 4%-5% (from 3.5%-4.5%), operating income guidance to 7%-8.5% (from 6%-8%), and EPS to $2.80-$2.87 (from $2.75-$2.85).

Management guided Q3 operating income growth of just 2%-4% and EPS of $0.62-$0.64, urging investors to view Q2 and Q3 together (averaging ~10% OI growth per quarter) due to concentrated price reinvestment.

Guidance now absorbs more than $2 billion of incremental fuel-related costs and roughly 20 basis points of OI headwind from the Vibe acquisition, with a softer consumer noted especially in June as gas prices topped $4.
High-margin profit drivers surged, with global advertising up 38% (Walmart Connect up 43%), U.S. marketplace up 52%, and global membership income up nearly 17% at all-time highs.

Walmart U.S. deployed over 11,000 rollbacks (up from ~7,200 in Q1), driving transaction and unit growth and strong food-category share gains, though management warned it creates a temporary deflationary effect with a lagged sales benefit.

In-store comps declined low single digits due to health and wellness, but stores now fulfill 80% of e-commerce orders; automation now serves 3,100 U.S. stores and processes over 50% of e-commerce fulfillment volume, and CapEx was raised to ~4% of net sales.

# Walmart (WMT) — Q2 FY2027 Earnings Preview

**Report date:** August 20, 2026 · **Event:** Thursday, Aug 20, 2026, results at 6:00 a.m. CDT (7:00 a.m. ET / 11:00 UTC), call at 7:00 a.m. CDT — **pre-market**
**Quarter:** Q2 FY2027 (quarter ended July 31, 2026) · **Hosts:** John Furner (CEO), John David Rainey (CFO)
**Last price:** $114.30 (Aug 19 close, −0.78%); $114.62 pre-market · **Mkt cap:** ~$910–920B · **P/E (TTM):** ~40x · **Fwd P/E:** ~38x

> ⚠️ **Timing caveat:** the scheduled event (11:02 UTC) is essentially now. Everything below is pre-print positioning; as of the last quote I could verify (6:37 a.m. ET pre-market), the release was not yet out. Verify against the actual 8-K before trading on it.

---

## 1. Consensus Estimates

| Metric | Consensus / Guide | YoY | Source & date |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Revenue** | **$186.7–186.8B** | **+5.3%** (vs $177.4B) | Street consensus via CNBC / TradingKey, Aug 19–20, 2026 |
| **Adj. EPS** | **$0.73–0.74** | **+7.4% to +8.8%** (vs $0.68) | Barchart ($0.73) / CNBC & BofA ($0.74), Aug 19–20, 2026 |
| Company guide: net sales | +4% to +5% cc | — | Walmart Q1 FY27 release, May 21, 2026 |
| Company guide: adj. operating income | **+7% to +10% cc** | — | Walmart Q1 FY27 release, May 21, 2026 |
| Company guide: adj. EPS | $0.72–$0.74 | — | Walmart Q1 FY27 release, May 21, 2026 |
| Walmart U.S. comp ex-fuel | ~3.5% (BofA) vs 4.1% in Q1 | decel. | BofA Securities preview, Aug 2026 |
| FY27 revenue guide | $731.1–738.2B | +3.5–4.5% cc | Reaffirmed at Q1, May 21, 2026 |
| FY27 adj. EPS guide | $2.75–$2.85 | +6–8% op. income | Reaffirmed at Q1, May 21, 2026 |

**Estimate dispersion note:** published consensus differs slightly by vendor ($0.73 vs $0.74 EPS; $186.73B vs $186.8B revenue). Consensus sits **at the top of management's own $0.72–0.74 guide** — i.e., the Street is already underwriting a high-end print, which removes the cushion an in-line number would normally provide.

---

## 2. The Setup: What Actually Happened Last Quarter

Q1 FY27 (reported May 21, 2026) was a *beat that the stock hated*. Shares fell **~7.3%** on the day and **−12% over May**, from a record close of $134.20 on May 19.

| Q1 FY27 actual | Result |
|---|---|
| Total revenue | $177.75B, **+7.3%** reported / **+5.9% cc** |
| Operating income | **+5.0%** reported; adj. **+5.1% cc** |
| Walmart U.S. comp (ex-fuel) | **+4.1%** (beat ~3.9% consensus) |
| Sam's Club U.S. comp (ex-fuel) | **+3.9%**, transaction/unit-led |
| International net sales | **+10.1% cc** (higher reported on FX) |
| Global eCommerce | **+26%** |
| Global advertising | **+37%** (Walmart Connect U.S. +44% ex-VIZIO) |
| Global membership fee income | **+17.4%** |
| Operating cash flow / FCF | $4.7B / **−$1.9B** |
| Fuel drag on operating income | **~(250) bps** |

Why the stock fell anyway: Q2 EPS guide ($0.72–0.74) landed below the ~$0.75 Street bar, FY27 revenue guidance ($731.1–738.2B) came in far under the ~$748B modeled, and FY27 adj. EPS ($2.75–2.85) undershot ~$2.91. Management flagged consumer pressure from fuel. Critically, **Walmart did not raise any FY guidance at Q1** — a break from last year, when the Q2 FY26 print came with a full-year raise.

---

## 3. Key Metrics to Watch — Ranked

**1. Adjusted operating income growth (cc) vs. the +7–10% guide — this is the print.**
Q1 delivered **+5.1% cc OI on +5.9% cc sales** — *negative* operating leverage. The Q2 guide asks for **+7–10% OI on +4–5% sales**, a 3–5pt positive spread. That is a ~4–5 point swing in leverage in one quarter. The bridge has to come from advertising, membership, marketplace/fulfillment mix, and an assumed easing of the fuel drag.

**2. The fuel math — the biggest identifiable risk to that bridge.**
Q1 (Feb 1–Apr 30) captured only ~two months of war-elevated fuel (the US–Iran conflict began Feb 28) and still cost 250bps of OI growth. **Q2 (May 1–Jul 31) carried a full three months at higher levels.** Diesel is running **$5.40/gal vs $3.70 a year ago** and gasoline $4.07 vs $3.20 — record August highs, with WTI at $85.34 and Brent $91.19 on Aug 19. *This is my inference from the calendar and the price tape, not company disclosure* — but if the fuel headwind held at 250bps or widened, the 7–10% OI guide is difficult without an offset. Watch for management quantifying the Q2 fuel bps.

**3. Walmart U.S. comp ex-fuel, and the traffic/ticket split.**
BofA models ~3.5% vs 4.1% in Q1. Bernstein flagged a comp slowdown from **lapping last year's tariff-driven price increases** — a pricing, not a volume, decel. Traffic-led comps = share gains and a quality beat; ticket-led = inflation pass-through and a lower-quality beat. Note reported comps *including* fuel get an artificial lift from pump prices — insist on the ex-fuel line.

**4. The high-margin flywheel: advertising, membership, marketplace.**
Global ads +37% and membership fee income +17.4% in Q1 are the entire margin story. Any deceleration in Walmart Connect below ~30% undermines the "structural margin expansion" thesis that justifies a ~40x multiple on a low-single-digit-growth retailer.

**5. FY27 guidance action — raise, reaffirm, or trim.**
Walmart has now gone one quarter without a raise. A raise (or a push to the top half of $2.75–2.85) is the single biggest upside unlock; a trim toward the low end confirms the bear case that the margin algorithm broke.

*Secondary:* gross margin ex-fuel, inventory growth vs sales, FCF recovery after the −$1.9B Q1, back-to-school commentary, low-income cohort behavior and trade-down (fuel inflation is a *share* tailwind for Walmart even as it's a *cost* headwind), and eCommerce profitability.

---

## 4. Scenario Analysis

| Scenario | Prob. | Revenue | Adj. EPS | Key driver | Stock reaction |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Bull** | 25% | ~$188.5B (+6.3%) | **$0.76–0.78** | WMT U.S. comp ≥4.5% traffic-led; ads ≥35%; **OI growth at/above +10%** with fuel drag narrowing; **FY27 EPS guide raised** toward/above $2.85 | **+4% to +7%** |
| **Base** | 45% | $186.5–187.5B (+5.2–5.7%) | **$0.74–0.75** | Comp 3.8–4.2%; eComm low-20s%; OI +7–8% (low end of guide); FY27 guidance **reaffirmed/narrowed**, not raised | **−2% to +2%** |
| **Bear** | 30% | ≤$185.5B (+≤4.6%) | **$0.71–0.72** | Comp ≤3.4% on tariff-price lapping; **OI growth ≤6%, below guide** on a wider fuel/distribution drag; FY27 adj. EPS cut to $2.70–2.78 | **−5% to −9%** |

**What each requires operationally.** *Bull:* the fuel headwind compresses below ~150bps and ad/membership dollars flow through at incremental margin — Rainey quantifying a smaller-than-expected fuel bps drag and using the words "raising our outlook" is the tell. *Base:* Walmart hits the algorithm's floor — sales in-line, OI at the bottom of 7–10%, and management holds the year "given continued macro uncertainty," the exact language used in May. *Bear:* comps decelerate *and* margin misses simultaneously; the tell is any framing of fuel as "persistent" or a second consecutive quarter of OI growth trailing sales growth.

**Historical calibration.** Over 19 prints in five years, one-day reactions were positive 53% of the time (only **42% over the last three years**), median +4.6% up / −4.5% down, with a range of +7.0% to −11.4%. Recent tails are real: **−7.3% last quarter**, **+9.4% in August 2024**. Walmart has beaten revenue consensus **25 straight quarters** — a revenue beat is priced in and, on its own, is not a catalyst.

---

## 5. Catalyst Checklist

1. **Adj. OI growth (cc) vs. +7–10%** — the leverage question; a sub-7% print with an in-line EPS is still a bear outcome.
2. **FY27 adj. EPS guide vs. $2.75–2.85** — no raise is now the base case; a raise re-rates the stock, a trim breaks it.
3. **Walmart U.S. comp ex-fuel vs. ~3.5–4.0%**, decomposed into traffic vs. ticket.
4. **Advertising vs. +37% / membership fee income vs. +17.4%** — the margin-mix engine that supports the multiple.
5. **Fuel bps quantification + low-income consumer commentary** — the swing factor for both this quarter's margin and 2H guidance credibility.

---

## 6. Trading Setup

| | |
|---|---|
| Last / pre-market | $114.30 / $114.62 |
| 52-week range | $95.42 – $135.16 |
| From record close | **−14.8%** (vs $134.20 on May 19, 2026) |
| **Options-implied move** | **~±4.6%** (Bloomberg) / 4.56% (Barchart) ≈ **±$5.25 → $109.05–$119.55** |
| Market value at risk | ~$42B |
| Positioning skew | **Bearish** — put/call ~1.56x on the Aug 21 expiry (one vendor cites 2.53x); downside strikes clustered ~$110.5–112 |
| Sell-side | 26 Buy / 3 Hold (TipRanks, 29 analysts); avg PT ~$138–140; BofA $144, Bernstein $142 |
| Valuation | ~40x TTM / ~38x forward vs. 10-yr median ~31x — still a premium, but ~4 turns cheaper than the May peak |

**Read.** The implied ±4.6% is roughly *fair* against the realized median absolute move (~4.5%), so options are not obviously cheap or rich; the edge is in direction, not vol. The setup is asymmetric in an underappreciated way: the stock has already given back 15% and four multiple turns since May, and positioning is skewed short — which cushions a merely-in-line print and means the **bear case largely needs a guidance cut, not just a soft quarter**, to produce another −7%. Conversely, because consensus already sits at the *top* of management's EPS guide and revenue beats are a 25-quarter formality, the bull case requires an actual **FY27 guidance raise**. My concern with the base case is the fuel arithmetic in §3.2: the calendar worked against Walmart in Q2, and the +7–10% OI guide was set before diesel made new records.

---

*Analysis prepared from publicly available sources; consensus figures are vendor-aggregated and vary slightly by provider. Company-reported figures are sourced to Walmart IR. Not investment advice.*

content: Q2 sales rose 5.7% year-over-year to $47.9 billion, with total comp sales up 1.7% and U.S. comps up 1.3%, both exceeding company expectations.
Adjusted diluted EPS was $4.92, up 5.1% from $4.68 a year ago, while GAAP diluted EPS rose to $4.79 from $4.58.
Comps accelerated through the quarter (total: May +1.2%, June +1.5%, July +2.3%), and management said Q3 has started consistent with Q2 demand trends.
The company received $730 million in IEEPA tariff refunds late in June, of which $685 million reduced Q2 cost of goods sold and boosted gross margin by roughly 145 basis points.
Excluding the tariff refund, gross margin faced about 120 basis points of pressure (60 bps from higher fuel, energy, and input costs, and 60 bps from GMS/Mingledorff acquisition mix).
Management expects tariff refunds to be fully offset by unplanned cost pressures over the year, creating a Q2-to-Q3 timing shift, with Q4 gross margin expected to be roughly flat year-over-year.
Comp average ticket rose 2.8% while comp transactions fell 1%, with big-ticket transactions over $1,000 up 2.4% amid continued weakness in large discretionary projects.
Online sales grew 11% year-over-year, marking the fifth straight quarter of double-digit growth, supported by higher traffic and conversion.
13 of 16 merchandising departments posted positive comps, Pro outperformed DIY, and SRS comped above the company average with positive comps across all verticals.
The company reaffirmed fiscal 2026 guidance of flat-to-2% comp growth, ~2.5%-4.5% total sales growth, ~33.1% gross margin, 12.4%-12.6% operating margin, and flat-to-4% EPS growth.

| Departments positive | 9 of 16 · Digital +10%+ |
| Stock reaction | **+0.88%** |

**FY2026 guidance (reaffirmed at Q1):** total sales +2.5–4.5% · comps ~flat to +2% · GM ~33.1% · op margin 12.4–12.6% (adj. 12.8–13.0%) · tax 24.3% · diluted and adj. EPS growth ~flat to +4% (i.e., adj. **$14.69–$15.28**) · capex ~2.5% of sales · ~15 new stores.

### The two pieces of arithmetic that matter

**(a) H1 EPS is running *down*, and the guide requires a sharp H2 reversal.**
H1 adj. EPS at consensus = $3.43 + $4.71 = **$8.14**, versus $8.24 in H1 FY2025 — **down 1.2% Y/Y**. Prior-year H2 adj. EPS was $6.45. To reach:

- the **low end** ($14.69, flat): H2 must do $6.55, **+1.6% Y/Y**
- the **Street** (~$15.00): H2 must do $6.86, **+6.4% Y/Y**
- the **high end** ($15.28, +4%): H2 must do $7.14, **+10.7% Y/Y**

The full-year number is almost entirely an H2 story, and the Street sits closer to the top of the range than the bottom. This is the single largest source of asymmetric downside on the print.

**(b) Q2 is the last full quarter of GMS inorganic lift.**
GMS closed **September 4, 2025**. Q2 FY2026 (May–early Aug) carries a full inorganic contribution; Q3 FY2026 laps it about a month in. H1 total sales growth of ~+4.8% is running *above* the top of the +2.5–4.5% full-year guide — meaning H2 reported sales growth mechanically decelerates to roughly +0.5–2.5% unless comps accelerate. Any investor reading Q2's headline +4.9% as underlying momentum is mis-framing the quarter.

---

## 3. Key Metrics to Watch (ranked)

1. **U.S. comparable sales and the transaction line.** Ticket has carried comps for four-plus quarters while transactions decline. Placer.ai puts HD's Q2 visits at **–0.3% Y/Y** vs. Lowe's **+0.4%** — traffic stabilized, not recovering. If comp transactions are worse than Q1's –1.3%, the "engagement is fine, projects are deferred" narrative weakens.
2. **Gross margin delta vs. Q1's –75bp.** McPhail guided Q2 pressure to continue but "not quite to the degree" of Q1, with H2 returning to roughly flat. Q2 GM better than about –65bp validates the FY 33.1% bridge; worse than –75bp breaks it.
3. **Big-ticket (>$1,000) comp transactions.** +0.8% in Q1. This is the cleanest read on discretionary project demand with the 30-year mortgage at ~6.67–6.69% and housing turnover near multi-decade lows.
4. **Guidance action.** Reaffirm vs. narrow vs. trim. Given (a) above, a reaffirmation of the *full* range is a modest positive; narrowing to the lower half is the most likely negative.
5. **SRS/GMS organic trend and Pro cross-sell.** SRS comps were slightly negative in Q1 on roofing. HD targets ~$400M of Pro cross-sell this year with ambition to roughly double. Any quantified progress is an underappreciated bull lever.
6. **Section 338 tariff commentary** (see catalyst 4).
7. **Interim-management tone** — first call without Decker.

---

## 4. Scenario Analysis

| Scenario | Prob. | Revenue | Adj. EPS | Comps | What has to happen | Stock reaction |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Bull** | 20% | ~$48.0B (+6%) | **$4.85–4.95** | +2.0–2.5% | Comp transactions inflect toward flat; GM decline narrows to <50bp as GMS mix drag moderates; SRS organic returns positive; management points to lower half→upper half of FY EPS range or explicitly backs ~$15.00 | **+4% to +7%** |
| **Base** | 55% | ~$47.4–47.6B | **$4.72–4.78** | +1.0–1.5% | Ticket +2.5–3%, transactions –1% to –1.5%; GM ~–60bp, in line; FY guide reaffirmed unchanged; H2 recovery framed as "on track" without new proof points | **–1% to +2%** |
| **Bear** | 25% | ~$46.8–47.1B | **$4.55–4.62** | flat to +0.5% | Transactions deteriorate past –2%; GM down ≥85bp on tariff/fuel/mix; SRS comps stay negative; FY comps trimmed to "flat to +1%" and adj. EPS to "flat to +2%"; tariff cost flagged but unquantified | **–5% to –8%** |

**Management commentary that signals each:** *Bull* — "sequential improvement in comp transactions," "gross margin pressure moderating as expected," a raised Pro cross-sell number. *Base* — "in line with our expectations," "underlying demand relatively similar" (Decker's Q1 phrasing). *Bear* — "we now expect the lower end," "greater than anticipated cost pressure," or refusal to quantify Section 338 exposure.

**Historical calibration:** over five years HD has closed positive on 12 of 20 prints (60%; 67% over three years), with a **median positive move of +1.8% and a median negative move of –3.2%**. Realized moves have been muted lately — last four averaged ~3.0% absolute (Q3 FY25 **–6.0%**, Q4 FY25 **+2.0%**, Q1 FY26 **+0.9%**). The one big drawdown came on a *guidance* disappointment, not an EPS miss. That is the shape of the risk here.

---

## 5. Catalyst Checklist

1. **Comps vs. ~+1.2% and, more importantly, the transaction line vs. –1.3%.** Ticket-led comps are lower quality; the market has tolerated them while traffic held flat. Placer data says traffic is flat-to-slightly-down, so a transaction print worse than –2% would break the pattern.
2. **Full-year guidance: reaffirm, narrow, or trim.** The buy-side wants the unchanged $14.69–$15.28 range reaffirmed. Consensus at ~$15.00 requires H2 adj. EPS +6.4% Y/Y off an H1 that is down 1.2%. Narrowing to the lower half is effectively a ~4% cut to Street EPS and is the most probable route to a –5%+ day.
3. **Section 338 tariffs — the timing is unusually hostile.** Proclamations signed July 20, 2026 impose an additional **50% duty on a wide list of Canadian goods effective 12:01 a.m. ET August 19, 2026 — the morning after this print** — including plywood and wood-based panels, furniture, and cement, applied regardless of CUSMA preference. HD will be asked to quantify COGS exposure and its pricing response on a call held before the duties are even live. An unquantified answer is a bear-case accelerant; a credible sizing plus a mitigation plan removes an overhang.
4. **Gross margin bridge to 33.1%.** With H1 GM tracking ~32.9% at consensus, H2 must run ~33.3% — roughly flat-to-up Y/Y — leaving essentially no cushion for tariff or fuel cost inflation.
5. **Narrative/governance: first report under interim leadership.** Announced August 12, 2026, Decker is on temporary medical leave with return expected "within the next few months." Ann-Marie Campbell (SEVP) runs day-to-day; **CFO Richard McPhail oversees financial management *and* the Pro subsidiaries**; lead director Greg Brenneman chairs the board. Watch for reduced willingness to make forward commitments — interim managements historically reaffirm rather than raise. Any hint the leave is longer or more permanent than framed is a separate, non-fundamental risk.
6. **Read-across obligation: Lowe's reports August 19 pre-market** ($26.14B / $4.22 EPS consensus, revenue +9% on M&A, EPS –3%). LOW's Q2 traffic was +0.4% vs HD's –0.3%; a soft HD comp followed by a firm LOW comp turns a cyclical story into a share-loss story.

---

## 6. Trading Setup

- **Implied vs. realized:** options price ±4.2–4.3% (~$14); the last four realized moves averaged ~3.0%. On raw base rates, the straddle looks ~30–40% rich. But the median *down* move (–3.2%) is nearly 2x the median *up* move (+1.8%), and the historical worst case (–6.0%) came on guidance — the exact risk live here.
- **Positioning skew:** put/call on the August 21 expiry at **2.06**, a bearish tilt. Sentiment is defensive into the print, which cuts both ways: it lowers the bar for a relief rally on a clean reaffirm, and it means downside is partly pre-hedged.
- **Technical/valuation frame:** $338.86 vs. a recent peak near $358 and a ~$374 average PT; –2.2% YTD but ~+15% over three months, so the stock has already priced in a good chunk of an H2 recovery at ~21.8x forward.

**How I'd frame the risk/reward:** the setup is negatively skewed at the guidance line and roughly neutral at the EPS line. Consensus EPS is very likely met or modestly beaten (four-quarter average surprise +1.6%, ESP +1.35%); the FY guide is where the money is made or lost, and the H1/H2 arithmetic plus a tariff step-up landing the next morning argues the risk is a narrowed range rather than a raise. If you are long into the print, the cheapest expression of that view is owning downside protection rather than trimming, given how much bearish positioning is already in the August 21 puts.

---

### Caveats
Consensus figures are as of Aug 13–17, 2026 and will drift into the print. The comp-sales consensus is my derivation, not a sourced figure — verify against your own contributor consensus before trading on it. Q2 FY2025 gross and operating margin percentages are approximations implied by full-year guidance and modeled Y/Y deltas rather than figures pulled from the Q2 FY2025 release (the IR PDF would not parse); the Y/Y *changes* are the sourced part. Scenario EPS and stock-reaction ranges are my estimates.

# Salesforce (CRM) — Q2 FY2027 Earnings Preview

*Prepared 26 Aug 2026 · Report lands today, 4:01 PM ET / 20:01 UTC, after the close · Call ~5:00 PM ET*

---

## 1. Event & Consensus

**Quarter:** Q2 FY2027, ended 31 July 2026

| Metric | Consensus | Company Guide (27 May 2026) | Y/Y | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | **$11.33B** | $11.27–11.35B | +10.6% | Street sits at the upper half of the guide |
| Non-GAAP EPS | **$3.27** | $3.25–3.27 | +12.4% | Consensus = top of guide, unmoved for 60 days |
| cRPO growth (cc) | ~13% | ~13% cc | — | Q1 was $33.6B, +14% nominal / +13% cc |
| Non-GAAP op. margin | ~34% | FY27: 34.3% | +~150bps | Q1 printed 34.8% (+250bps) |
| GAAP op. margin | ~20–21% | FY27: 20.6% | — | Q1: 21.1% (+130bps) |

**Consensus source/date:** Zacks / TipRanks / aggregator composites as of 24–26 Aug 2026 (~53 covering firms; $3.27–3.28 EPS, $11.330B revenue). Estimates are effectively anchored to the guide — the Street has done no independent work above it.

**Standing FY27 guidance:** Revenue $45.9–46.2B (+11%, 10–11% cc, ~3pts Informatica); non-GAAP EPS $14.06–14.12; non-GAAP OM 34.3%; GAAP OM 20.6%; OCF/FCF growth 4–5%.

---

## 2. The Setup in One Paragraph

CRM is ~$209, **down ~21–22% YTD** but **up ~40% off late-June lows**, at ~$181B market cap and roughly **14.8x** the FY27 non-GAAP EPS guide midpoint. The sell side has spent August marking price targets *to* the stock rather than above it — Citi $187→$204 (Neutral, 24 Aug), Wells Fargo $200→$205 (Equal Weight), UBS $185→$210 (Neutral) — while Morgan Stanley and KeyBanc downgraded earlier on the failure of Agentforce bookings to show up in cRPO. JPMorgan resumed at Overweight, $250. Options price a **~7–8% move** against a **3.35% average absolute move** over the last four prints. That gap is the whole trade: the market is paying up for a narrative resolution, not an EPS number.

---

## 3. Key Metrics to Watch — Ranked

**1. cRPO growth in constant currency (the only number that matters).**
Q1: +13% cc. Guide: ~13% cc. This is the metric on which Morgan Stanley and KeyBanc downgraded, and the one Oppenheimer's Brian Schwartz flagged (he wants 13–14% in *Q3* to underwrite H2 reacceleration). Agentforce ARR growing triple digits while cRPO grows 13% is the bear case in a single sentence. **≥14% cc is a clean beat; ≤12% cc breaks the H2 reacceleration story management sold in May.** Watch the Q3 cRPO guide as much as the Q2 print.

**2. Organic growth ex-Informatica.**
Management said Informatica adds **>4pts to Q2 growth (>$400M)** on last year's $10.24B base. Backing that out of consensus:

| | Q1 FY27 (actual) | Q2 FY27 (at consensus) |
|---|---|---|
| Reported growth | +13% (+12% cc) | +10.6% |
| Informatica contribution | $444M | ~$410–430M |
| **Implied organic growth** | **~+8.7%** | **~+6.6%** |

That is a ~2pt organic deceleration hiding inside a 10.6% headline. Caveat: Q1 organic was flattered by professional-services timing (CFO's own attribution), and ~1pt of FX tailwind runs through both. Still, **the core franchise is decelerating toward mid-single digits and M&A is masking it.** Any comment quantifying organic ex-Informatica growth will be scrutinized.

**3. Agentforce / Data 360 / AI-and-data ARR — and its composition.**
Q1: **$3.4B AI + data ARR**, Agentforce ARR **>$1B** (some trackers put it at $1.2B, +205% Y/Y — treat the higher figure as unverified). Critically, management said ~**50% of agentic and Data 360 bookings came from existing customers expanding**. The bear question is whether Agentforce is *new* wallet or a reallocation of existing Salesforce spend. Watch for: AI+data ARR ≥$4B, new-logo contribution disclosure, and any detail on Agentic Work Unit (AWU) consumption billing converting to recognized revenue. Slack is the sleeper — ACV +80% Y/Y, Active Work Units +350% Q/Q, and involved in nearly half of $1M+ wins in Q1.

**4. FY27 guidance action.**
Revenue: raise vs. narrow vs. maintain. In May they raised the FY midpoint; a *maintain* here would be read as an admission that H2 organic reacceleration isn't materializing. EPS: the guide is arithmetically conservative (see §4) and a raise to ~$14.40+ is the low bar.

**5. Margin, cash, and buyback.**
FY27 OCF/FCF growth of only **4–5%** is the soft underbelly — well below revenue growth, diluted by Informatica. Q1 FCF was $6.6B (seasonal peak). Non-GAAP OM should track toward 34.3% FY. The **$25B ASR** (half of the $50B authorization) cut Q1 diluted shares ~10% Y/Y (103M shares) and added **$0.23 to non-GAAP EPS**; the second $25B tranche is the swing factor on any EPS guidance raise.

---

## 4. The Sandbag Math — Why $3.27 Is Not the Real Bar

This is the most important calibration in the note.

| | Non-GAAP EPS | vs. Street |
|---|---|---|
| Q4 FY26 actual | $3.81 | est. $3.05 → **+25%** |
| Q1 FY27 actual | $3.88 | est. $3.12 → **+24%** |
| Q2 FY27 guide | $3.25–3.27 | consensus $3.27 |

Four straight EPS beats, the last two by ~25%. Now check the full-year arithmetic: FY27 guide midpoint **$14.09** − Q1 actual **$3.88** − Q2 guide **$3.26** = **$6.95 across H2, or ~$3.48/quarter**. Management's own annual guide embeds *zero* carry-through from a 24% Q1 beat. That is a deliberate sandbag.

**Implication:** published consensus of $3.27 is a guide-echo, not a forecast. The functional buy-side whisper is materially higher — plausibly **$3.55–$3.80** on EPS (ASR share count + margin flow-through) and **$11.40–11.45B** on revenue. **An in-line-to-slightly-above EPS print of $3.30–3.40 will trade as a miss.** Do not confuse the headline beat with the reaction.

---

## 5. Scenario Analysis

| Scenario | Revenue | Non-GAAP EPS | cRPO (cc) | Key Driver | Stock Reaction |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Bull** (25%) | ~$11.45B (+11.8%) | $3.80–3.95 | **+15%** | Agentforce converts to contracted backlog; FY27 rev raised to $46.1–46.3B, EPS to $14.50+; AI+data ARR >$4B with new-logo disclosure | **+7% to +12%** |
| **Base** (50%) | $11.36–11.40B (+11%) | $3.50–3.65 | **+13%, in line** | Solid beat on a sandbagged guide; FY27 revenue narrowed upward, EPS raised on ASR; Q3 cRPO guided ~13% | **−2% to +4%** |
| **Bear** (25%) | $11.28–11.32B (low half) | $3.25–3.40 | **≤12%** | Organic ex-Informatica <6%; Q3 cRPO guided below 13%; FY27 revenue merely maintained; Commerce/Tableau/Marketing softness widens | **−8% to −15%** |

**What each requires operationally:**

- **Bull** — Net-new AOV outpacing expansion AOV (the CFO's stated H2 leading indicator) *and* showing up in cRPO; Informatica bookings sustaining the double-digit reacceleration seen two quarters post-close; Slack and Data 360 attach offsetting Commerce/Tableau. Management tell: an explicit organic-growth number, a quantified new-logo AI cohort, and confidence language on H2 rather than "pipeline."
- **Base** — Everything works except cRPO acceleration. Management tell: reiterating "second-half organic reacceleration" without new proof points, and leaning on ARR milestones instead of backlog. This is the most likely outcome and the one where a 24% EPS beat still gets sold.
- **Bear** — cRPO decelerates, or the Q3 cRPO guide implies deceleration. Management tell: attributing softness to "deal timing," widening the list of soft products beyond Commerce and Tableau, or introducing FX/macro as an excuse. A guidance *maintain* on revenue after May's raise is the single most damaging possible action.

**Historical calibration.** Over 20 quarters, CRM's one-day post-earnings return has been positive exactly 50% of the time; median positive **+3.8%**, median negative **−4.4%**; extremes **+11.5%** (Dec 2023) and **−19.7%** (May 2024). Recent prints: May 2026 **−0.8%**, Feb 2026 **+4.0%**, Dec 2025 **+3.7%**, Sep 2025 **−4.9%**, May 2025 **−3.3%**. The February print is the template for the current regime — a ~25% EPS beat produced roughly a 4% move, and the stock still finished the following months lower. **Beats have not been sufficient for four quarters running; guidance and the AI-monetization proof have been the swing factor.**

---

## 6. Catalyst Checklist

1. **cRPO cc growth vs. ~13% guide / ~14% whisper** — the direct rebuttal (or confirmation) of the Morgan Stanley/KeyBanc downgrade thesis. Highest-beta line in the release.
2. **Q3 FY27 cRPO guidance** — Oppenheimer's stated 13–14% threshold. A sub-13% guide invalidates H2 reacceleration regardless of the Q2 print.
3. **FY27 revenue guidance action** — raise (bull), narrow-up (base), maintain (bear). Buy-side expects a raise to at least $46.0–46.2B; a maintain is the tell that organic is deteriorating.
4. **Organic growth ex-Informatica, disclosed or derivable** — ~6.6% at consensus vs. ~8.7% in Q1. Management is unlikely to volunteer this; analysts will force it on the call.
5. **AI monetization quality** — AI+data ARR trajectory from $3.4B, Agentforce from >$1B, and specifically the **new-logo vs. expansion split** and AWU consumption-to-revenue conversion. Narrative shift risk: any repositioning of Agentforce pricing, further restructuring (GAAP OM was already adjusted for restructuring in the FY guide), or new M&A after Informatica would be read as offense-through-acquisition and pressure the multiple.

---

## 7. Trading Setup

| | |
|---|---|
| Spot | **~$209** (24–26 Aug) |
| YTD | **−21% to −22%** |
| From late-June low | **+~40%** |
| Market cap | ~$181B |
| Multiple | **~14.8x** FY27 guide midpoint ($14.09) |
| Dividend yield | ~0.84% |
| Options-implied move | **~7–8%** (sources span 6.5% / 7.4% / 8.0%) |
| Avg. absolute move, last 4Q | **3.35%** |
| Straddle breakevens (~7.5%) | **~$193 / ~$225** |
| Sell-side | Moderate Buy — 25 Buy / 9 Hold / 2 Sell; avg PT **~$239** |
| Recent PT moves | Citi $204 (N), WFC $205 (EW), UBS $210 (N), JPM $250 (OW) |
| Institutional ownership | >80% |

**Read-through.** The implied move is roughly **2x** realized experience — premium is expensive and the setup favors sellers of volatility over buyers of it, unless you have a differentiated cRPO view. The stock has already run 40% off the lows into the print, which removes the "bombed-out expectations" cushion that supported the February and December reactions. Simultaneously, the concentration of *Neutral-rated* price targets at $204–210 — precisely at spot — means the sell side has repriced the stock without endorsing it; there is little institutional conviction to absorb a cRPO disappointment. Asymmetry skews modestly negative into the number, with the caveat that the EPS bar (§4) is genuinely low and a cRPO acceleration would find a lightly-positioned, heavily-shorted-narrative tape.

---

## Data Quality Notes

Please read these before trading off the above:

- **Primary sources were inaccessible.** The Salesforce Q1 FY27 press release, the SEC 8-K exhibit, the Q1 investor deck, and several preview articles (Benzinga, Invezz, TechTimes) returned HTTP 403 or exceeded fetch limits. **All figures here are from secondary aggregators and a transcript summary — none were verified against the primary filing.** Confirm the Q1 baseline and guidance numbers against the 8-K before committing capital.
- **Unresolved conflicts in the source data:**
  - *Agentforce ARR*: ">$1B" (earnings call) vs. "$1.2B, +205% Y/Y" (aggregator). Used the conservative figure.
  - *Put/call ratio*: 1.06 (bearish skew, Aug-28 expiry) vs. 0.85 (bullish). Contradictory; not resolved.
  - *Implied move*: 6.5% / 7.38% / 8.01% across three sources.
  - *Average price target*: $238.94 (TipRanks) vs. $252 (Barchart).
  - *Forward multiple*: one source cites "~20x forward earnings"; that is irreconcilable with $209 spot on the $14.06–14.12 FY27 guide, which yields ~14.8x. The same source quoted a "$2.35 Q2 EPS consensus," which is wrong on any basis — I used its price and options data only, and discarded its derived statistics.
  - *Q4 FY26 reaction*: "−1.2% after-hours" vs. "+4.0% one-day." The one-day series is internally consistent with the 3.35% four-quarter average, so I used it.
- **Scenario probabilities and whisper-number ranges in §4 and §5 are my estimates**, derived from the guidance arithmetic and the two-quarter beat pattern — they are not survey data. Actual buy-side whisper surveys were not available from public sources.

No files were written and nothing was published.

**Q4 FY26 guide is the actual event:** consensus revenue **$34.9B** (high end $37.0B), EPS **$3.87**, with Morgan Stanley modeling $34.8B and **AI revenue $21.2B (+32% q/q)**.

**The arithmetic that matters:** Management's FY26 AI target of **$56B** minus H1 AI (~$18.8B) minus Q3 guide ($16B) leaves **exactly ~$21B for Q4**. The $56B target has effectively pre-committed the Q4 AI guide. Anything below ~$21B is a self-inflicted cut, not a "conservative guide."

---

## 2. Key Metrics to Watch — Ranked

1. **Q4 AI semiconductor guide vs. ~$21B.** The single highest-beta number. Below $20B breaks the $56B FY26 target and calls FY27's ">$100B" into question.
2. **Gross margin at/above ~74%, and the FY27 GM framing.** Q2's selloff was a margin-mix event as much as a guidance event — XPUs/TPUs carry structurally lower GM than AI networking and software. Bulls need Hock Tan to re-anchor on *operating* margin (67%) and dollar gross profit, not the GM percentage.
3. **AI bookings/backlog.** Q2 disclosed **$30B of AI bookings vs. $10.8B shipped** and a **~$73B AI backlog over 18 months**, with visibility "into 2028." A backlog print materially above $73B is the cleanest bull catalyst; a flat/down backlog is the cleanest bear catalyst.
4. **Infrastructure software $8.9B (+31%).** This requires a sharp re-acceleration from +1% (Q1) → +9% (Q2). Software missed StreetAccount by ~$140M last quarter and was a proximate cause of the –12.6% reaction. Highest risk of a "quiet miss" inside a headline beat.
5. **OpenAI Phase 1 / Microsoft financing.** The ~$18B, 1.3GW first phase reportedly stalled on Broadcom requiring Microsoft to commit to ~40% offtake. Any concrete update — or refusal to comment — moves the FY27/FY28 narrative. Volume XPU deployment is still guided to 1GW+ in 2027.
6. **Customer concentration / Google diversification.** Tan conceded last quarter that Google is dual-sourcing ASICs. Watch for a 7th named XPU customer (current six: Google, Meta, Anthropic, OpenAI, Fujitsu, ByteDance) and any color on Google TPU share.
7. **FCF conversion ≥40–46% of revenue** and capacity/supply commentary for 2028–29, which was still under negotiation as of June.

## 3. Scenario Analysis

| Scenario | Q3 Rev / EPS | Q4 Guide | Key Driver | Stock Reaction |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Bull (~25%)** | $30.2B+ / $3.35+ | **≥$36B rev, AI ≥$22B** | AI backlog re-rates above $73B; FY26 AI raised above $56B; GM held ≥74.5%; software ≥$8.9B; OpenAI Phase 1 confirmed funded | **+9% to +15%** ($403–$425) |

**Operationally, what each requires**
- **Bull:** Tan raises the FY26 AI number *and* frames FY27 above $100B with a specific figure. Historically he only raises when supply is locked — so a raise doubles as a supply-secured signal. Needs GM stabilization language ("74% is the trough").
- **Base:** The "beat-and-reiterate" pattern that has now sold off twice in three quarters. Reaffirming $56B/$100B is priced in.
- **Bear:** The setup has an asymmetry — Q4 AI is arithmetically pinned at ~$21B, so there is very little room to *positively* surprise on the guide without raising FY26 outright, while a shortfall reads as a cut.

**Historical reaction calibration**

| Report | Implied | Actual close | Peak |

---

## 4. Catalyst Checklist

- [ ] **Q4 AI revenue guide vs. $21B** — the FY26 $56B target's residual; below $20B = guide-down in disguise.
- [ ] **Q4 total revenue vs. $34.9B consensus** — bull line ~$36B, bear line ≤$33B.
- [ ] **Non-GAAP GM ≥74% and Q4 GM commentary** — is 74% the trough or the new glide path? Watch whether Tan pivots the framing to operating margin/gross profit dollars.
- [ ] **AI backlog vs. $73B / bookings vs. $30B** — the quarter's most under-modeled disclosure.
- [ ] **Infrastructure software vs. ~$8.9B (+31%)** — a repeat miss after Q2 rewrites the "VMware is the margin ballast" thesis.
- [ ] **OpenAI Phase 1 status + Microsoft offtake** — and any 7th XPU customer.
- [ ] **FY27 ">$100B"** — raised, quantified, or merely reaffirmed. Reaffirmation alone disappointed in June.

---

## 5. Trading Setup

- **Price/technicals:** ~$369.7 close, sitting *on* the 200-day EMA ($369.07) — below the 20-EMA ($378) and 50-EMA ($386). RSI14 43, MACD histogram –1.67 (deteriorating). Support $364, resistance $373. ATR14 $12.48. Entering the print on weak momentum at a decisive technical level: a bear print has an air pocket below the 200-EMA.
- **Positioning:** stock has round-tripped 26% off its high and only +7% YTD despite ~84% revenue growth — this is *not* the June setup, when shares had rallied 14% in the week into the print. Expectations are visibly lower, which cuts the tail risk relative to Q2.
- **Sell-side:** consensus "Strong Buy," average PT ~$520–526 (range $216–$675); J.P. Morgan reiterated Buy, PT $580. EPS revisions positive (25 up / 9 down over 30 days). NTM P/E ~23x on one third-party model — cheap versus the growth rate, which is the core of the bull case and why the debate is margin quality, not multiple.
- **Options view:** ±8.1–8.7% implied against a 10-yr median of ±5.8% looks *rich vs. median* but **cheap vs. the last four prints**, three of which exceeded the implied move. Straddle buyers have been paid in 62% of the last 16. Given the guide is arithmetically pinned and the tape is technically weak, **skew favors long downside convexity (put spreads) over outright straddles**; selling premium here is picking up nickels in front of a name that has twice dropped >11% on beats.
- **Skew of my base case:** in line with the market's ±8%, but distributionally fat-tailed to the downside — the modal outcome is a small move, the tail outcome is a large negative one.

---

# Oracle Corp. (ORCL) — Q1 FY2027 Earnings Preview

**Report date:** September 10, 2026 · **Event:** Today, 4:05pm ET (20:05 UTC), after the close · Call at 5:00pm ET
**Stock:** ~$155 (down ~4% intraday Sept 10) · **Market cap:** ~$460B · **Consensus PT:** ~$242 (42 analysts)

> **The setup in one line:** The quarter itself is largely de-risked — guidance is tight, prediction markets put an EPS beat at ~80%, and Oracle has beaten on EPS consistently. The stock is not trading on the P&L. It is trading on **RPO direction, capex, and who is funding the backlog.** ORCL is ~55% below its $345.72 high set exactly one year ago on the Q1 FY26 print, and the market has spent 2026 repricing the same backlog it celebrated in 2025.

---

## 1. Consensus Estimates

| Metric | Consensus | Company Guidance (given June 10, 2026) | Year-Ago (Q1 FY26) | Implied Y/Y |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Total revenue** | **$19.13B** | +27% to +29% | $14.93B | **+28%** |

*Sources: sell-side compilations via investingLive, 24/7 Wall St. and Finbold, Sept 7–10, 2026; guidance from Oracle's Q4 FY26 release, June 10, 2026. Segment splits marked "implied" are derived from the consolidated cloud guide, not separately published consensus.*

**Full-year FY27 (the number that actually matters):** $90B revenue (+34%) and $8.05 non-GAAP EPS (+18%), both reaffirmed in June. Q1 at $19.1B is only **21% of the full-year target**, requiring ~$23.6B average across Q2–Q4. This guide is severely back-half loaded, which is why the Q2 guide and the FY27 reaffirmation carry more weight than the Q1 print.

---

## 2. Key Metrics to Watch — Ranked

**1. RPO — direction, not level (highest importance).** Ended Q4 at **$638B, +363% Y/Y, +$85B Q/Q**, of which roughly **$300B is OpenAI** and $75B relates to prepaid/customer-supplied GPU hardware. Only 12% converts within 12 months; another 34% in months 13–36. With ~$19B of revenue burning off and no confirmed new mega-deal, **RPO can print flat-to-down without anything being wrong** — but the market will not read it that way. A sequential decline below ~$600B is the single most dangerous outcome tonight. Watch for new logos: Q4 had $67B of AI infrastructure bookings across four customers each above $8B, and diversification away from OpenAI is worth more than the headline number.

**2. OCI revenue vs. the 58–64% cloud guide.** The guide implies OCI roughly **doubling Y/Y to ~$7.4B** and stepping up 25–30% sequentially off Q4's $5.8B (+93%). This is a **capacity-delivery question, not a demand question** — GPU utilization was 97.5% in Q4. A miss here means data centers landed late, not that customers left. Confirm whether the shortfall (if any) is megawatts or bookings.

**3. Capex, free cash flow and financing.** FY26 capex was **$55.7B** against $32B operating cash flow, producing **negative FCF of $23.7B**. FY27 is guided to **~$70B net cash outlay** (~$90–95B gross before prepayments), funded by ~$40B of debt and equity including a $20B ATM equity program. Management said in June it does *not* expect to raise additional debt in calendar 2026 — **any walk-back of that statement is the bear trigger.** Expect Q1 FCF around negative $8–12B.

**4. Gross margin trajectory.** CFO Hilary Maxson flagged that gross margins "step down because of data center ramp timing," with infrastructure margins improving as capacity reaches full contractual revenue. Any incremental OCI margin disclosure would be a genuine positive surprise — the absence of segment-level cloud margin detail is a live investor complaint.

**5. Balance sheet and credit.** ~$117B of Oracle paper sits in the Bloomberg US high-grade index (largest non-financial issuer). CDS widened above 125bp — post-2009 highs — and Barclays moved the debt to underweight in November 2025 on BBB- risk. **The credit market is now the marginal price-setter for the equity.**

**Secondary:** MultiCloud database revenue (+404% in Q4, bookings +325%), Q2 FY27 guide, first full year under co-CEOs Clay Magouyrk and Mike Sicilia, and any commentary on the reported OpenAI IPO delay.

---

## 3. Scenario Analysis

| Scenario | Prob. | Revenue | Non-GAAP EPS | RPO | Key Driver | Stock Reaction |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Bull** | 25% | $19.5B+ (+30%) | $1.80+ | **$700B+** | New non-OpenAI multi-GW deal signed; cloud >64%; capex held at $70B net; FCF crossover timeline given | **+10% to +18%** → $170–183 |
| **Base** | 45% | $19.1–19.3B | $1.74–1.78 | **$620–670B** | In-line quarter, cloud ~60%, FY27 $90B/$8.05 reaffirmed, capex unchanged, no new financing | **−4% to +6%** → $149–164 |
| **Bear** | 30% | $18.8–19.0B (low end/miss) | ≤$1.72 | **<$600B** | Cloud below 58% on DC delays; RPO down sequentially or OpenAI contract re-scoped; capex raised; incremental debt/equity announced | **−15% to −25%** → $116–132 |

**What each requires operationally:**

- **Bull:** Oracle must show the backlog is *broadening*, not just aging. That means a named new hyperscale-class customer, OCI landing at or above ~$7.6B proving capacity came online on schedule, and management putting a date on peak capex. Listen for "we do not need to return to the debt markets" repeated verbatim.
- **Base:** Everything lands inside the guide. The stock does little because an in-line quarter resolves none of the funding debate — this is the highest-probability outcome and the lowest-payoff one for anyone positioned directionally.
- **Bear:** Any of three things — RPO falls, capex rises, or financing expands. Note these are not independent; a capex raise and a financing raise arrive together. Watch for softened language around OpenAI's ramp beginning in calendar 2027.

**Historical calibration:** The last four reactions averaged **16.1% in absolute terms**, range 8.5% to 36.0%. Sept 2025 (Q1 FY26): **+36%**, the largest one-day gain in decades, on the $455B RPO reveal. March 2026 (Q3): **~+10%**. June 2026 (Q4): **−8.5% at the close, −12.9% intraday**, on a beat — the stock fell on the $40B financing plan, not the numbers. December 2025 (Q2) reaction direction unconfirmed in available sources. **The June print is the template: Oracle can beat and still sell off.**

---

## 4. Catalyst Checklist

1. **RPO vs. $638B** — the entire AI-infrastructure narrative is marked to this number. Sequential direction, plus any disclosure of non-OpenAI concentration, determines the multiple.
2. **Cloud revenue growth vs. 58–64%** — the buy-side whisper sits at the **upper half (~62%+)** given Q4's 93% OCI print. In-line at 58% will read as a miss.
3. **FY27 $90B / $8.05 reaffirmation** — with Q1 only 21% of the annual target, any softening of the full-year language is disproportionately damaging.
4. **Capex guide and the "no more debt in CY2026" commitment** — a raise above $70B net outlay, or new financing, is the single fastest path to the bear case.
5. **OpenAI commentary** — roughly half the backlog. Reports of missed OpenAI targets and a delayed IPO have already pressured the stock; management addressing counterparty risk directly would be a positive, and dodging it would not.

---

## 5. Trading Setup

**Read-through:** The options market is pricing **~11–12% against a 16% historical average** — implied vol looks cheap relative to realized earnings-day behavior, and the bear tail here (RPO decline plus a financing surprise) is fatter than a symmetric distribution implies. Long-volatility structures screen better than directional exposure. The gap between a $155 spot and a $242 consensus target is not a valuation opportunity so much as evidence that **sell-side models have not been marked to the credit market's view of the funding plan.**
